discovery: Theoretical prediction and establishment of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order

nominees.name: Libor Šmejkal
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, Germany; Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Tomáš Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic; University of Nottingham, UK

motivation: Using spin-group symmetry analysis, Šmejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova showed that collinear magnets do not split into ferromagnets and antiferromagnets alone. They identified a third, symmetry-distinct phase: altermagnets. These have compensated magnetic order with zero net magnetization, yet their electronic bands are strongly spin-split with d-, g- or i-wave symmetry. The splitting comes from crystal symmetry, not relativistic spin-orbit coupling. This organizing principle reclassified many known materials and predicted unconventional anomalous Hall and spin-splitter effects. In 2024 several independent groups confirmed the predicted spin-split bands directly by photoemission in MnTe and CrSb, and the magnetic domains have since been imaged. The result is a textbook example of theory preceding experiment. It is changing how we think about magnetic order, spintronics without stray fields, and how magnetism interplays with superconductivity. It is a deep, general and rigorously verified addition to the classification of quantum phases of matter.
